front: A full-wave bridge rectifier is driven by a transformer secondary with peak voltage \(V_m = 18\ \text{V}\). The four rectifier diodes are silicon with a \(0.7\ \text{V}\) drop each. Find the peak voltage delivered to the load.
explanation: In a bridge rectifier, two diodes conduct in series on each half-cycle, so two forward drops are subtracted. \[V_{L,\text{peak}} = V_m - 2V_D = 18 - 2(0.7) = 16.6\ \text{V}.\]

front: A light-emitting diode with forward drop \(V_F = 2\ \text{V}\) is to operate at \(I = 15\ \text{mA}\) from a \(5\ \text{V}\) supply using a series current-limiting resistor. Find the required resistance.
explanation: The series resistor drops the difference between the supply and the LED voltage while carrying the LED current. \[R = \frac{V_S - V_F}{I} = \frac{5 - 2}{0.015} = 200\ \Omega.\]

front: A \(5\ \text{V}\) Zener shunt regulator is fed from a \(15\ \text{V}\) source through a series resistor \(R_s = 200\ \Omega\) and drives a load \(R_L = 1\ \text{k}\Omega\). Assuming the diode maintains \(5\ \text{V}\), find the current in the Zener diode.
explanation: Current through the series resistor: \[I_{R_s} = \frac{15 - 5}{200} = 50\ \text{mA}.\] Load current: \[I_L = \frac{5}{1000} = 5\ \text{mA}.\] KCL at the regulator node gives \[I_Z = I_{R_s} - I_L = 50 - 5 = 45\ \text{mA}.\]

front: A \(5\ \text{V}\) Zener diode in a shunt regulator carries \(45\ \text{mA}\). Find the power dissipated in the diode.
explanation: Power dissipated equals the diode voltage times its current. \[P_Z = V_Z I_Z = (5)(0.045) = 0.225\ \text{W} = 225\ \text{mW}.\]

front: A full-wave rectifier operating from a \(60\ \text{Hz}\) line uses a capacitor filter \(C = 1000\ \mu\text{F}\) and supplies a load drawing \(I_L = 100\ \text{mA}\). Estimate the peak-to-peak ripple voltage.
explanation: For a full-wave rectifier the capacitor is recharged twice per line cycle, so the ripple frequency is \(f_r = 2(60) = 120\ \text{Hz}\). \[V_{r(pp)} \approx \frac{I_L}{f_r C} = \frac{0.1}{(120)(1000\times10^{-6})} = 0.83\ \text{V}.\]

front: A silicon BJT with \(\beta = 100\) and \(V_{BE} = 0.7\ \text{V}\) uses fixed base bias: \(V_{CC} = 10\ \text{V}\) connects to the base through \(R_B = 465\ \text{k}\Omega\). Find the base current and the collector current.
explanation: Base loop (KVL): \[I_B = \frac{V_{CC} - V_{BE}}{R_B} = \frac{10 - 0.7}{465\times10^{3}} = 20\ \mu\text{A}.\] In the active region, \[I_C = \beta I_B = 100(20\ \mu\text{A}) = 2\ \text{mA}.\]

front: A BJT voltage-divider bias circuit has \(V_{CC} = 12\ \text{V}\), \(R_1 = 40\ \text{k}\Omega\) (from \(V_{CC}\) to base), \(R_2 = 20\ \text{k}\Omega\) (base to ground), \(R_C = 2\ \text{k}\Omega\), \(R_E = 1\ \text{k}\Omega\), and \(V_{BE} = 0.7\ \text{V}\). Neglecting base current, find \(I_C\) and \(V_{CE}\).
explanation: Divider (base) voltage: \[V_B = V_{CC}\frac{R_2}{R_1+R_2} = 12\cdot\frac{20}{60} = 4\ \text{V}.\] Emitter voltage and current: \[V_E = V_B - V_{BE} = 3.3\ \text{V},\quad I_C \approx I_E = \frac{3.3}{1000} = 3.3\ \text{mA}.\] Collector-emitter loop: \[V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C(R_C + R_E) = 12 - (3.3\ \text{mA})(3\ \text{k}\Omega) = 2.1\ \text{V}.\]

front: The common-base current gain of a BJT is \(\alpha = 0.98\). Find the common-emitter current gain \(\beta\).
explanation: The current gains are related by \[\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{0.98}{1 - 0.98} = \frac{0.98}{0.02} = 49.\]

front: An NMOS transistor operating in saturation has \(k_n'\,(W/L) = 1\ \text{mA/V}^2\) and threshold voltage \(V_t = 1\ \text{V}\). If \(V_{GS} = 3\ \text{V}\), find the drain current.

An NMOS device with \(k_n'\,(W/L) = 0.5\ \text{mA/V}^2\) and \(V_t = 1\ \text{V}\) has \(V_{GS} = 3\ \text{V}\), a drain supply \(V_{DD} = 10\ \text{V}\), and drain resistor \(R_D = 2\ \text{k}\Omega\) (source grounded). Find \(I_D\) and \(V_{DS}\), and verify the operating region.
explanation: Assume saturation: \[I_D = \tfrac{1}{2}(0.5\ \text{mA/V}^2)(3 - 1)^2 = 1\ \text{mA}.\] Drain voltage: \[V_{DS} = V_{DD} - I_D R_D = 10 - (1\ \text{mA})(2\ \text{k}\Omega) = 8\ \text{V}.\] Since \(V_{DS} = 8\ \text{V} \ge V_{GS} - V_t = 2\ \text{V}\), the transistor is in saturation, confirming the assumption.

front: An ideal op-amp is configured as an inverting amplifier with feedback resistor \(R_f = 120\ \text{k}\Omega\) and input resistor \(R_{\text{in}} = 20\ \text{k}\Omega\). For an input of \(0.5\ \text{V}\), find the output voltage.
explanation: Inverting closed-loop gain: \[A_v = -\frac{R_f}{R_{\text{in}}} = -\frac{120}{20} = -6.\] Output voltage: \[V_{out} = A_v V_{in} = -6(0.5) = -3\ \text{V}.\]

front: An ideal op-amp non-inverting amplifier has feedback resistor \(R_f = 90\ \text{k}\Omega\) and a grounded resistor \(R_1 = 10\ \text{k}\Omega\). For an input of \(0.4\ \text{V}\), find the output voltage.
explanation: Non-inverting closed-loop gain: \[A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1} = 1 + \frac{90}{10} = 10.\] Output voltage: \[V_{out} = A_v V_{in} = 10(0.4) = 4\ \text{V}.\]

front: An ideal inverting summing amplifier has feedback resistor \(R_f = 10\ \text{k}\Omega\). Its inputs are \(V_1 = 1\ \text{V}\) through \(R_1 = 10\ \text{k}\Omega\) and \(V_2 = 2\ \text{V}\) through \(R_2 = 5\ \text{k}\Omega\). Find the output voltage.
explanation: Summing the input currents at the virtual-ground node: \[V_{out} = -R_f\left(\frac{V_1}{R_1} + \frac{V_2}{R_2}\right) = -(10\ \text{k}\Omega)\left(\frac{1}{10\ \text{k}\Omega} + \frac{2}{5\ \text{k}\Omega}\right).\] \[V_{out} = -(10\ \text{k}\Omega)(0.1\ \text{mA} + 0.4\ \text{mA}) = -5\ \text{V}.\]

front: A BJT is biased at \(I_C = 1\ \text{mA}\) with \(\beta = 100\) and thermal voltage \(V_T = 25\ \text{mV}\). Find the small-signal transconductance \(g_m\) and the base input resistance \(r_\pi\).

A common-emitter amplifier has transconductance \(g_m = 25\ \text{mA/V}\) and collector resistor \(R_C = 8\ \text{k}\Omega\), with \(r_o \gg R_C\) and no emitter degeneration. Find the mid-band small-signal voltage gain.
explanation: The common-emitter mid-band voltage gain is the product of transconductance and collector resistance: \[A_v = -g_m R_C = -(0.025\ \text{S})(8000\ \Omega) = -200.\] The minus sign reflects the \(180^\circ\) phase inversion of the stage.

front: An NMOS transistor in saturation has \(k_n'\,(W/L) = 2\ \text{mA/V}^2\) and is biased at an overdrive voltage \(V_{OV} = V_{GS} - V_t = 1\ \text{V}\). Find its small-signal transconductance \(g_m\).
explanation: For a MOSFET in saturation the transconductance is \[g_m = k_n'\frac{W}{L}(V_{GS} - V_t) = (2\ \text{mA/V}^2)(1\ \text{V}) = 2\ \text{mA/V}.\]

front: A forward-biased diode carries a DC current \(I_D = 0.5\ \text{mA}\). With ideality factor \(n = 1\) and thermal voltage \(V_T = 25\ \text{mV}\), find the diode's small-signal (dynamic) resistance.
explanation: The dynamic resistance is the reciprocal of the slope of the diode I-V curve at the operating point: \[r_d = \frac{n V_T}{I_D} = \frac{(1)(25\ \text{mV})}{0.5\ \text{mA}} = 50\ \Omega.\]

front: An ideal op-amp difference amplifier is built with matched resistor ratios \(R_f/R_1 = 5\) on both the inverting and non-inverting sides. The inputs are \(V_1 = 1.2\ \text{V}\) (inverting) and \(V_2 = 1.5\ \text{V}\) (non-inverting). Find the output voltage.
explanation: For a balanced difference amplifier the output depends only on the input difference: \[V_{out} = \frac{R_f}{R_1}(V_2 - V_1) = 5(1.5 - 1.2) = 5(0.3) = 1.5\ \text{V}.\]
